title: 10.3 Using Chords

icans: I can use congruent chords to find arc measures.
I can use a diameter that is perpendicular to a chord to find lengths.
I can use the fact that congruent chords are the same distance from the center.

vocab: a segment whose ____________ are on a circle
a line that is perpendicular to a segment at its ___________
Distance from a point to a line
the length of the ________________ segment from the point to the line

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: find the center by folding

blocks.p: Draw a chord on your paper circle. Fold so its endpoints match and crease. Repeat with a second chord. Mark where the creases cross.

head: Distance from the crossing point to the circle: 1st place
2nd place
3rd place

blocks.p: The crease of a chord always passes through the ______________ of the circle.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Congruent Corresponding Chords Theorem: in the same circle or congruent circles, two minor arcs are congruent if and only if their corresponding _______________ are congruent.

blocks.stem: In circle O, A̅B̅ ≅ C̅D̅ and m(arc AB) = 105°. Find m(arc CD).

notes: Perpendicular Chord Bisector Theorem: if a diameter of a circle is perpendicular to a chord, then the diameter _______________ the chord and its arc.

blocks.stem: Circle O has a radius of 13. Chord A̅B̅ is 5 units from the center. Find AB.

notes: Perpendicular Chord Bisector Converse: if one chord is a perpendicular bisector of another chord, then the first chord is a _______________.

blocks.stem: Chord C̅D̅ is the perpendicular bisector of chord A̅B̅. The radius of the circle is 13, and CD = 6x − 4. Find x.

notes: Equidistant Chords Theorem: in the same circle or congruent circles, two chords are congruent if and only if they are _______________ from the center.

blocks.stem: Chords A̅B̅ and C̅D̅ are each 5 units from the center of the circle. AB = 4x + 3 and CD = 6x − 7. Find CD.
Only the edge of a round garden is left. Explain how to find its center using chords.
A circle has a radius of 10. A chord is 12 units long. How far is the chord from the center?
Two chords are the same distance from the center of a circle. Their lengths are 7x − 1 and 5x + 9. Find x and the length of each chord.

tickets.stem: In one circle, chords P̅Q̅ and R̅S̅ are congruent. m(arc PQ) = 80°. Find m(arc RS).
A circle has a radius of 17. A chord is 8 units from the center. How long is the chord?
A diameter is perpendicular to chord A̅B̅ at M. AB = 18. Find AM.
